I shut down the enterprise tier today.

Eighteen months ago I thought enterprise was the obvious path. Bigger logos, bigger contracts, fewer customers to support. What actually happened: three pilots, two security questionnaires with 400 questions each, and one procurement process that outlasted the champion who started it.

Meanwhile the $29/month customers kept paying, kept emailing feature ideas, and kept referring their friends.

I am not saying enterprise is wrong. I am saying it was wrong for a one-person company with no sales motion. Lesson filed.

Hiring my first contractor this week after 14 months solo. Writing down what I am afraid of so I can laugh at it later:

1. They will see how messy the codebase is.
2. I will spend more time explaining than building.
3. I will like having a teammate too much and overhire.

Number 1 is definitely going to happen. https://example.com/blog/first-hire

Small thing that changed my week: I stopped answering support email in the morning. Mornings are for the one feature that moves the number. Support happens at 4pm, batched, with coffee. Response times went from 2 hours to 6. Nobody complained. Not one person.
